hospital_name: UW Medicine (Harborview Medical Center, UW Medical Center, Airlift Northwest, UW Physicians, UW Medicine Primary Care)

evidence.quote: 0% - 300% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) for a 100% financial assistance discount

tiers.description: Facility services only with discharge dates on or after July 1, 2022, at Harborview Medical Center and UW Medical Center; 75% financial assistance discount
Facility services only with discharge dates on or after July 1, 2022, at Harborview Medical Center and UW Medical Center; 50% financial assistance discount

evidence.quote: 351% - 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) for a 50% financial assistance discount

asset_test.details: Assets are not considered for financial assistance eligibility; they may be considered for Medicaid eligibility.

evidence.quote: UW Medicine does not take assets into consideration for determining Financial Assistance eligibility.
A patient may apply for financial assistance at any time prior to the account receiving a court judgement.

presumptive_eligibility: UW Medicine may waive income requirements, documentation, and verification if Financial Assistance eligibility is obvious.
how_to_apply: Complete a Confidential Financial Information (CFI) Form with supporting documentation; documents available at uwmedicine.org/financialassistance or through Financial Counseling or Patient Financial Services.
warnings: No fixed application deadline stated; policy says a patient may apply any time before a court judgement on the account (not a day count from a start date). The 15 business day period applies to returning application materials for collections purposes.

The 75% and 50% discount tiers apply only to facility services at Harborview Medical Center and UW Medical Center with discharge dates on or after July 1, 2022; other entities get free care up to 300% FPL only.
Financial assistance is generally secondary to third-party coverage; insured patients may qualify for remaining balances after coverage is exhausted.
Residency requirement not mentioned in the policy; it only notes assistance for out-of-state patients in identifying Medicaid programs.
Income is determined as of the date of service or at application if made within two years of service.
